inputs.original_text:
Look at what happens when authority collapses and weak leadership leaves ordinary people to suffer in endless, unresolved cycles of violence. We are supposed to believe some ceasefire was announced in Gaza five months ago, but the reality on the ground shows that security and order are completely absent. As 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five currently displaced in Deir al-Balah, rightly points out about the daily reality there: “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.” 

When civic structures and strong governance fail, it is the family unit that bears the ultimate burden, stripped entirely from their prewar existence as life becomes dark and brutal. This is the tragic cost of weakness and chaos. What we need is an absolute commitment to strong borders, national security, and decisive action that restores stability, rather than endless violence that shatters communities and destroys the foundations of orderly society.
inputs.modified_text:
Look at the devastating human cost of this ongoing crisis, where displaced communities are left completely unprotected and vulnerable. We are told about a ceasefire announced in Gaza five months ago, but the reality on the ground shows the absolute failure to protect ordinary people. As 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five currently displaced in Deir al-Balah, powerfully describes the daily reality: “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.” 

When institutional structures collapse and basic rights are denied, it is marginalized families who bear the ultimate burden, stripped entirely from their prewar existence as life becomes dark and brutal. This is the tragic cost of systemic neglect and ongoing violence that shatters communities and destroys the foundations of society, leaving the vulnerable to suffer without adequate protection or recourse.

rationales.relation_drift: The modified text shifts responsibility from weak leadership and failed governance toward systemic neglect and lack of protection, while preserving the reported violence.
rationales.contradiction_drift: The modified text contains no meaningful internal contradiction.
